Stop heat loss, handle gently, and rewarm the body core without burning skin. Use this order, and reassess after any major change. Move out of wind and wet, replace wet clothing, and insulate above and below. Warm the chest, neck, armpits, and groin with wrapped warm packs or shared body heat. Protect frostbitten tissue from pressure and refreezing; evacuate serious cases. Do not rub frostbite, use direct fire, give alcohol, or thaw tissue that may refreeze.

Use the least contaminated available source and still treat it for germs. Use this order, and reassess after any major change. Prefer a known safe supply, then clearer moving water collected upstream from camps, livestock, roads, or waste. Avoid water with fuel sheen, chemical smell, toxic algae, dead animals, mine drainage, or industrial runoff. Collect where the bank is stable and you cannot be swept into the water. Boiling and ordinary filters cannot make chemically contaminated or salty water safe.

Create a controlled visible signal without starting a wildfire or poisoning shelter occupants. Use this order, and reassess after any major change. Prepare the site, extinguishing material, and escape path before ignition. Use three small fires or add damp green material only after a stable fire is controlled and local conditions allow. Extinguish fully if wind rises, the signal is no longer needed, or control weakens. Do not light a signal fire during a ban, extreme fire weather, or where sparks can escape.

Reduce animal contact, inspect before reaching, and secure every food or scented item. Use this order, and reassess after any major change. Watch where hands and feet go around rocks, logs, brush, and stored gear. Wear footwear and use repellent, nets, and clothing appropriate to local disease risks. Shake out clothing and bedding and keep camp away from nests or obvious animal paths. Do not handle or attempt to kill a snake; many bites occur during handling.

Move away from fire spread and heavy smoke while avoiding steep, fuel-filled escape routes. Use this order, and reassess after any major change. Call emergency services when possible and follow official evacuation routes. Move toward a large cleared area, water edge, road, or already burned area when that is the safest reachable option. Cover nose and mouth from ash, stay low in cleaner air, and keep skin covered. Do not try to outrun a fast fire uphill or shelter in dense vegetation, a tent, or a vehicle surrounded by burning fuel.
